elements.element: Customer is not prohibited from participating in competing or similar projects or otherwise dealing with alternatives to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 expressly provides that the Company “shall not participate in any project similar to the Site” for the specified products.

elements.element: Vendor is not granted an exclusive or sole-provider right that restricts Customer’s use of other providers.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 grants HDI “the exclusive right” to use the Deerskin brand for the specified direct-to-consumer website.

elements.element: The exclusivity obligation is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Although “Deerskin Products” appears to be a defined category, the restriction also covers “products substantially similar to Deerskin Products,” including without limitation products of named companies and “companies similar” to them. Those open-ended extensions are not a defined product category.

elements.element: The exclusivity obligation lasts no longer than twelve (12) months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 applies only “during the twelve (12) month period commencing on the Effective Date.”

elements.element: The exclusivity obligation ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet a service level.
elements.evidence: The proviso states that all of Section 6.1 “shall terminate automatically upon HDI’s failure to meet any service level.”

elements.element: The exclusivity obligation ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet a delivery date.
elements.evidence: The same proviso states that Section 6.1 terminates automatically upon HDI’s failure to meet any “delivery date obligation.”

result.reason: The redline adds the required 12-month cap and automatic performance-based termination, but it does not fully satisfy the fallback because the restricted category remains open-ended through “substantially similar” products and products of undefined “similar” companies. It does not satisfy the preferred position because operative exclusivity remains. The changes leave the unrelated termination provisions intact and introduce no direct contradiction, but the redline is incomplete and retains vague scope language.
